# Objectives

Two scenarios will be compared to conduct a sensitivity analysis of BLM's carbonate system assumptions:

-   **Baseline**: Closed system, measured DIC as a BLM input variable

-   **Perturbed**: Open system, no DIC input. Instead, BLM estimates alkalinity by charge balance using pH and assuming in equilibrium with atmospheric partial pressure

# 1. Setup

Set working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/7. Sensitivity analyses")
```

Merge BLM output variables from the baseline conditions (closed system + HA 10%) and the perturbed scenario (open system + HA 10% ) from the clean Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet version 2 (pre-typology) and version 3 (with typological classification).

First, set the working directory and import each dataset as it's own object

```{r}
library(readxl)

# -------------------------------------------------
# 1) Set working directory
# -------------------------------------------------
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/7. Sensitivity analyses")

# -------------------------------------------------
# 2) Store file paths once (so you don't repeat them)
# -------------------------------------------------
file_master3 <- "C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/5. Cluster analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean3.xlsx"

file_master2 <- "C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean2.xlsx"

library(dplyr)

read_scenario <- function(path, sheet) {
  read_excel(path, sheet = sheet)
}

ha_10_cs <- read_scenario(file_master3, "HA 10% Closed System")
ha_10_os <- read_scenario(file_master2, "HA 10% Open System")
```

Add typology from ha_10_cs to each scenario

```{r}
library(dplyr)

typology_lookup <- ha_10_cs %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology) %>%
  distinct()

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>% 
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology, everything())

ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology, everything())

# quick sanity check: check if there are Sample_IDs that don't match (should be 0)
setdiff(ha_10_os$Sample_ID, ha_10_cs$Sample_ID)
```

# 2. Select variables of interest

Create a paired dataset

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Only retain BLM speciation mode output variables in nM and nmol/g for simplicity and consistency (one column per variable and all in same units of measurement)
ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Sample_ID,
    ends_with("_nM"),
    ends_with("_nmol_kg"),
    # log-transformed variables
    -starts_with("log_"),
    # Remove BLM predictors
    -"DOC_nM",
    -"Ca_nM",
    -"Mg_nM",
    -"Na_nM",
    -"K_nM",
    -"SO4_nM",
    -"Cl_nM",
    -"pH",
    -"DIC_nM",
    -"Zn_nM",
    -"Cu_nM",
    # Remove toxicity variables
    -ends_with("_tox_nM")
  )

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Sample_ID,
    ends_with("_nM"),
    ends_with("_nmol_kg"),
    # log-transformed variables
    -starts_with("log_"),
    # BLM predictors
    -"DOC_nM",
    -"Ca_nM",
    -"Mg_nM",
    -"Na_nM",
    -"K_nM",
    -"SO4_nM",
    -"Cl_nM",
    -"pH",
    -"DIC_nM",
    -"Zn_nM",
    -"Cu_nM",
    # Remove toxicity variables
   )

library(dplyr)

# Keep only Sample_IDs present in BOTH datasets

common_ids <- intersect(ha_10_cs$Sample_ID, ha_10_os$Sample_ID)

ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>%
  filter(Sample_ID %in% common_ids) %>%
  arrange(Sample_ID)

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>%
  filter(Sample_ID %in% common_ids) %>%
  arrange(Sample_ID)


# 2) Check that the numeric columns match

names_cs <- ha_10_cs %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% names()
names_os <- ha_10_os %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% names()

setdiff(names_cs, names_os)
setdiff(names_os, names_cs)
```

Create bioavailabile Zn variable in each dataset

```{r}
ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>%
  mutate(
    TBL_Zn_nmol_kg = BL_Zn_nmol_kg + BL_ZnOH_nmol_kg
  )

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>%
  mutate(
    TBL_Zn_nmol_kg = BL_Zn_nmol_kg + BL_ZnOH_nmol_kg
  )
```

# 3. Calculate sensitivity metrics

## i. Delta

Delta is the absolute change in a response variable from baseline to the perturbed BLM system assumptions; calculated as y_s2 - y_s1.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# 1. Separate the numeric data
num1 <- ha_10_cs %>% 
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric))

num2 <- ha_10_os %>% 
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric))

# 2. Subtract num1-num2
delta_dic <- ha_10_os %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID) %>%
  bind_cols(num2 - num1)

# 3. Check
delta_dic
```

Summarize delta by variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

summary_delta_dic <- delta_dic %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min    = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1     = ~quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean   = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3     = ~quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr    = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))) %>%
  # Pivot so it's a readable list instead of 500 columns wide
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), 
               names_sep = "_(?!.*_)") # Splits at the last underscore

# Check
head(summary_delta_dic)
```

## ii. Percent change

Percentage of delta

```{r}
# Multiply all numeric columns by 100
percent_change_dic <- delta_dic %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) * 100

# Check
head(percent_change_dic)
```

Check the distribution of the percent change

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

percent_change_dic %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of numeric variables in lrr_dic",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```

Summarize percent change by variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

summary_percent_change_dic <- percent_change_dic %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min    = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1     = ~quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean   = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3     = ~quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr    = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))) %>%
  # Pivot so it's a readable list instead of 500 columns wide
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), 
               names_sep = "_(?!.*_)") # Splits at the last underscore

# Check
head(summary_percent_change_dic)
```

## iii. Log response ratio (LRR)

LRR describes the effect size between the two BLM assumption outputs, calculated as

log10(y_s2) - log10(y_s1)

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Log transform each dataframe
log_ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), log10))

log_ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), log10))

# 2. Separate the numeric log-transformed data
log_num1 <- log_ha_10_cs %>% 
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric))

log_num2 <- log_ha_10_os %>% 
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric))

# 3. Subtract num1-num2
lrr_dic <- ha_10_os %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID) %>%
  bind_cols(log_num2 - log_num1)

# 4. Check
head(lrr_dic)
```

Check distribution of LRRs

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

lrr_dic %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of numeric variables in lrr_dic",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```

Summarize LRR for each numeric variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

summary_lrr_dic <- lrr_dic %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min    = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1     = ~quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean   = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3     = ~quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr    = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))) %>%
  # Pivot so it's a readable list instead of 500 columns wide
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), 
               names_sep = "_(?!.*_)") # Splits at the last underscore

# Check
head(summary_lrr_dic)
```

## iv. Robustness

To assess directional consistency in LRR, we'll summarize how many variables had a + or - LRR for each variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)

robustness_dic <- lrr_dic %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarize(across(everything(), list(
    positive = ~sum(.x > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    negative = ~sum(.x < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    zero = ~sum(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))) %>%
  # Pivot for readability
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), 
               names_sep = "_(?!.*_)") %>%
  # Add the ratio of positive/negative LRR values
  mutate(ratio = positive/negative)

# Check
head(robustness_dic)
```

# 4. Export SA results

Now we'll compile all of the output to one excel sheet

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Create a list of all output objects
dic_sa_list <- list(
  "Delta"              = summary_delta_dic,
  "Percent Change"     = summary_percent_change_dic,
  "Log Response Ratio" = summary_lrr_dic,
  "Robustness"         = robustness_dic
)

# Write into excel file
write.xlsx(dic_sa_list, file = "Carbonate_system_SA.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

# 5. Plots

Since the percent changes were not normally distributed, we'll plot the median and inter quartile ranges (IQRs) for each variable

## i. Percent change

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Pivot table: turn columns into rows
long_percent_change_dic <- percent_change_dic %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Value") %>%
  # Calculate the stats
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarize(
    median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # Sort variables by median value
  mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, median))
  
  
# 2. Plot
library(ggplot2)

pc_plot <- ggplot(long_percent_change_dic, aes(y = Variable, x = median)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = median)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = q1, xmax = q3), width = 0.25) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "red3", mid = "grey95", high = "steelblue4", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(x = "Percent Change (Median ± IQR)", y = NULL, 
       title = "Percent Change Summary for Zn BLM",
       subtitle = "Closed system to open system BLM") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)) + 
  guides(fill = "none")

# 3. Save plot

# Define output directory
out_dir <- "Plots of DIC SA"

# Create folder if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Save plot
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Percent_Change_DIC_SA.png"),
  plot = pc_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 8,
  units = "in",
  dpi = "print"
)
```

## ii. LRR

Since the LRRs were not normally distributed, we'll plot the median and inter quartile ranges (IQRs) for each variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Pivot table: turn columns into rows
long_lrr_dic <- lrr_dic %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Sample_ID, 
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Value") %>%
  # Calculate the stats
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarize(
    median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # Sort variables by median value
  mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, median))
  
  
# 2. Plot
library(ggplot2)

lrr_plot <- ggplot(long_lrr_dic, aes(y = Variable, x = median)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = median)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = q1, xmax = q3), width = 0.25) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "red3", mid = "grey95", high = "steelblue4", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(x = "LRR (Median ± IQR)", y = NULL, 
       title = "Log Response Ratio (LRR) Summary for Zn BLM",
       subtitle = "Closed system to open system BLM") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)) +

# 3. Save plot
out_dir <- "Plots of DIC SA"

  filename = file.path(out_dir, "LRR_DIC_SA.png"),
```
